summary: In major commercial spaceflight developments, SpaceX announced plans for a $100 billion launch site in Louisiana, as a new White House policy set a target to support 1,000 annual U.S. launches and reentries by 2030. Meanwhile, SpaceX achieved its 100th Falcon 9 launch of the year, setting a rocket-reuse record while outlining long-term plans to retire the workhorse launcher once Starship becomes operational. Aboard the International Space Station, astronauts Anil Menon and Sophie Adenot completed a spacewalk to repair the orbiting laboratory by replacing a failed video antenna. In defense and industry news, rocket startup Ursa Major announced a $2.3 billion deal to go public, Polish startup Ares Shield was hired to protect data center satellites using high-power microwave weapons, and the U.S. Navy revealed a new long-range air-to-air missile designated "Malice." Additionally, Hernandez-Baquero was sworn in as the Department of the Air Force space acquisition and integration lead. In civil space and science developments, NASA's Pandora mission began its study of exoplanets and host stars, NASA satellites successfully demonstrated GPS-free space navigation, and the Chandra X-ray Observatory released a new gallery of galaxy images. Looking ahead, skywatchers should watch for a 96 percent partial lunar eclipse taking place on Aug. 27–28.
